articles.title: LSU Fans Concerned Over Kiffin And LSU's Decision To Recruit Former NFL Players
articles.summary: The showdown between LSU and Clemson has been overshadowed by controversy
articles.body: The showdown between No. 11 LSU and Clemson was always going to be a showcase Week 1 game given Lane Kiffin's debut in the bayou. But few could have imagined the discussion surrounding the game would be anything like this. The heated on-field rivalry between two national powerhouses that share a stadium nickname (Death Valley) and mascot (Tigers) has been largely overshadowed by court cases involving NFL players returning to college football to use their final year of eligibility. Matt Moscona, a sports radio talk show host with 104.5 ESPN in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, said the issue has dominated the airwaves this week. He estimates that 10 of the 12 segments on his three-hour talk show on Thursday were devoted to the topic, while only one was about the actual game. He said LSU fans are genuinely worried. Not about Clemson, but about the long-term impact that Kiffin's desire to recruit and play former NFL players in defiance of SEC rules will have on the football program. "The phrase everyone here is using is, ‘Is the juice worth the squeeze?,’" Moscona said. "Why go through this big public ordeal to add a couple of backup players? Which is what we're talking about, quite honestly. The overriding sentiment is people are fearful of the punishments." He said that fear includes speculation that Kiffin might be suspended for ignoring SEC's stance, or even the Tigers being kicked out of the conference altogether after being a founding member in the early 1930s. "People here are wondering if we are really thinking about the long-term ramifications of playing a few backups," Moscona said. Kiffin recruited two of his former players at Ole Miss — defensive tackle Zxavian Harris and tight end Dae’Quan Wright — after both spent time with NFL clubs this offseason. That stirred up a hornets' nest, with the Southeastern Conference suing LSU in federal court this week and potentially tainting a partnership dating to the Depression. Several coaches have been outspoken against NFL players returning to college, including Clemson's Dabo Swinney who called the notion of ex-NFL players suiting up on Saturdays "embarrassing" for the sport. All four Power Four conferences last week reiterated their rules against pro players and some outlined stiff penalties including fines and suspensions. SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey testified that "the line between professional sports and college sports needs to be maintained," even in an era where top college players command million-dollar compensation packages through revenue sharing and NIL deals. Kiffin, one of the most outspoken and polarizing figures in college football long before his recruitment of NFL players, sees things a little differently than most in college football. He said he talked with LSU team leaders and all backed the idea of bringing in players who can help the Tigers — whether they tried out for NFL teams or not. He shrugged off the idea that it would wreck any final notion that college is meant for amateur athletes. "This is how it works at the next level," Kiffin said this week. "This is how the real world works." College Football Related StoriesRutgers Fan Goes Off After UMass Loss: 'I’m Done. I’m Canceling Everything'2026 College Football Week 1: Best Games To Watch This WeekendDeion Sanders Brings Out Receipts After Colorado's Stunning Georgia Tech Win Moscona noted that other teams have landed former NFL players including South Carolina, which recently signed kicker Ethan Sanchez after he attended camp with the San Francisco 49ers. He blames for the NCAA for not granting a blanket waiver to allow athletes from the 2022 high school class to return for a fifth year after changing its eligibility model in June. "The problem here is those players would have never left had they known they would have had another year of eligibility," Moscona said. "... The NCAA did not heed advice that lawsuits would follow. And, the lawsuits have followed. And now it's awful." Regardless of what happens, this is clearly not your average high-profile college season opener. LSU has a received a record number of requests — more than 900, according to the school — from media and VIPs. "I think that speaks volumes of the eyeballs on us and people wanting to be around the program and watch the program," Kiffin said. "All that is important nowadays. No. 1 is winning but after that you have a very marketable program." Reporting by The Associated Press.

articles.title: The Pac-12 Is Back: How Did We Get Here? Who Will Play In The Conference?
articles.summary: A look at the history of the Pac-12 and the team that will make up the new-look conference.
articles.body: Once the Washington Huskies' celebration of beating bitter rival Oregon in the 2023 Pac-12 Championship Game — and clinching a spot in the College Football Playoff — finally calmed down, an awkward reality began to set in. This was the end of Pac-12 football as we knew it. One of the oldest conferences in college sports, dating back to the formation of the Pacific Coast Conference in 1915, was about to disappear. Its demise had been years in the making, with the inability to secure and improve its media rights deal at the center of the problem. As name, image and likeness transformed college football, the premier programs knew they could no longer afford to fall behind the Big Ten and SEC. Washington, Oregon, UCLA and USC headed to the Big Ten. Reacting to their departure, Arizona, Arizona State, Colorado and Utah joined the Big 12. Left hanging, Cal and Stanford scurried to find a home in the ACC. The movement diminished the Pac-12 to a two-team conference of Washington State and Oregon State. Gone were the days of Pac-12 basketball tournaments in Las Vegas. The Apple Cup rivalry between Washington and Washington State moved to the beginning of the season. The tradition of staying up late to watch the ever-chaotic "Pac-12 After Dark" ended. Now, after two years of the Pac-12 conference essentially ceasing to exist, it's back. So back. The new-look Pac-12 in 2026 looks much different than it did in the past. There will still be rivalries, heated competition, and late-night shockers, but it's no longer viewed as a power conference. Now, a team must be ranked higher than every other Group of Six opponent in the final top 25 to reach the College Football Playoff. Another fun fact: Every Pac-12 football team has the word "State" in its name. The new members include five teams from the Mountain West — Boise State, Colorado State, Fresno State, San Diego State and Utah State — and one from the Sun Belt Conference, Texas State. They join Oregon State and Washington State to complete the eight-team Pac-12. The Broncos have long been one of the premier Group of Six programs, and now bring their famous blue field to the bright lights of the Pac-12. Fresno State and Utah State each qualified for bowl games in 2025, while Colorado State will look to turn things around under former UCLA coach Jim Mora. Texas State, meanwhile, has won a bowl game in each of the past three seasons. One wrinkle: Gonzaga will join the conference for college basketball, bringing the Pac-12 to nine members in that sport. The Bulldogs have qualified for the NCAA Tournament in each of the past 17 seasons, including trips to the national championship game in 2017 and 2021. The new-look Pac-12 might not have the luster or level of competition of its predecessor, but it should be one of, if not the, strongest Group of Six conferences in both football and basketball. articles.title: Former Cal softball player files lawsuit against university, female ex-coach over alleged sexual misconduct
articles.summary: Chelsea Spencer allegedly pressured a Cal softball player into a sexual relationship and cut her playing time, according to a new lawsuit filed in court.
articles.body: A former University of California, Berkeley softball player is accusing an ex-head coach of using her position of authority to pressure the player into a sexual relationship and allegedly threatening her playing time if she ended it. The complaint, filed Aug. 24 in Alameda County Superior Court and obtained by OutKick, alleges Cal failed to intervene and allowed Chelsea Spencer to remain as head coach for months after athletic department staff learned of the alleged relationship. Spencer ultimately stepped down last year in June, four months after agreeing to a multi-year contract extension. According to the lawsuit, a subsequent Cal investigation concluded that Spencer had violated campus policy regarding conflicts of interest in consensual relationships. The filing does not detail the dates when the probe started or ended. It also alleged Spencer was not cooperative in the process. SJSU VOLLEYBALL COACH'S ALLEGED ASSAULT VICTIM SPEAKS OUT FOR THE FIRST TIME SINCE ALLEGATIONS SURFACED In an email to OutKick on Friday, a Cal spokesperson declined to comment on the lawsuit or the school's investigation into Spencer. The former softball player retained the services of Slater Slater Schulman law firm. Gizem Gures, an attorney at the firm, referenced Cal’s reputation and its response to the investigation in a statement to USA Today Sports about the lawsuit. "Berkeley proudly holds itself out as the No. 1 public university in the world. That reputation comes with a responsibility to protect its students. As a Cal alum, it is deeply disappointing to see what our client experienced and how the University responded after its own investigation substantiated the conduct. Our client deserved better. Berkeley's students deserve better. The University needs to do better," the statement read. The complaint further alleges that Spencer’s advances toward the former player started in fall 2023, after the unnamed player joined the softball team as an incoming transfer. It says Spencer contacted her daily, via phone calls and text messages. Those communications eventually took on a romantic tone. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE At one point, Spencer allegedly told the player, "you’re so beautiful" and "your girlfriend is so lucky." The complaint further alleges that Spencer shared details about her personal life and gave gifts in the form of cash. Once the player effectively ignored the coach's messages, Spencer allegedly became angry and cut her playing time as punishment, the complaint claims. "When Plaintiff did not provide Spencer the attention she demanded, Spencer yelled at Plaintiff, treated her differently, and reduced or withheld Plaintiff's playing opportunities," the complaint states. "Plaintiff thus began to recognize, even before the relationship became sexual, that Spencer's personal demands and Spencer's authority as Head Coach were intertwined." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The former player argued that Spencer’s conduct and the university’s alleged negligence caused her severe emotional distress and forced her to end her collegiate softball career earlier than she would have otherwise. She is seeking a jury trial and damages for personal injuries and other losses.

articles.title: Judd Trump thrashes Zhao Xintong to reach last four of British Open
articles.summary: Judd Trump thrashes world number one Zhao Xintong 5-1 as he moves into the semi-finals of the British Open.
articles.body:
Judd Trump thrashed world number one Zhao Xintong 5-1 as he moved into the semi-finals of the British Open.

The Englishman will now face Aaron Hill or Jak Jones on Saturday, with Mark Selby taking on Liam Highfield in the other last-four encounter.

"When it goes down to two or one table it is a completely different set-up and you feel like the tournament comes alive," Trump said on Channel 5.

"In that kind of scenario I am so used to being out there and it gets the adrenalin going and it gets me more up for the fight especially against him [Zhao].

Earlier on Friday, Highfield had defeated teenage star Stan Moody 5-2, while Selby claimed a thumping 5-0 victory over Jack Lisowski.

And Trump delivered more of the same in the evening against the man who recently deposed him at the top of the rankings.

The 37-year-old, who has won 31 ranking titles, opened with a break of 101 and 57 to take the opening two frames before Zhao responded with a century of his own.

However, Trump restricted his Chinese opponent to just 29 points over the following three frames, while knocking in two further half-centuries to easily advance.

"[I was] probably a little more determined than normal," Trump added.

"In the past when I have lost the number one spot or people put other players as the favourite, you don't have that as number one and have that same demeanour of wanting to prove everyone wrong or that I'm the best."

articles.title: Sabalenka interrupts US Open match against Rakhimova over cannabis smell
articles.summary: World number one Aryna Sabalenka’s straight-sets US Open win against Kamilla Rakhimova stopped by smell of cannabis.
articles.body:
World number one Aryna Sabalenka had an unusual interruption during ⁠her US Open third-round ⁠match, stopping play to alert the umpire to a strong smell of cannabis drifting onto the Louis Armstrong Stadium court.

Sabalenka, who ⁠had made a fast start to go 3-0 ahead before securing a straight-sets win against Uzbekistan’s Kamilla Rakhimova, raised the issue during her second service game on Friday, pointing ⁠out the smell before play resumed.

“Someone is smoking weed,” top seed Sabalenka told umpire Eva Asderaki-Moore as she was serving 30-0 up. “Would you mind to… because it’s so strong.”

Sabalenka later told reporters she was not objecting to anyone enjoying themselves, but asked for the smoking ‌to be kept away from the court.

“I was like, Guys, you can do whatever, you can smoke whatever, you can relax as much as you can, but please to not do it around the tennis courts,” a smiling Sabalenka said. “It’s a bit tricky to handle that smell while you’re trying to compete at your best.”

The odour of cannabis has become a familiar — if unwelcome — feature at ⁠Flushing Meadows, with players complaining about the distraction in the ⁠past.

While smoking is not permitted inside the grounds, recreational cannabis is legal for adults 21 and older in New York, and smoke from people in the surrounding Flushing Meadows-Corona Park can drift into the tennis ⁠complex and onto the courts.

Sabalenka said she had smelled cannabis before during the tournament but never so strongly during a ⁠match, with Friday’s wind apparently carrying the odour into ⁠the stadium.

“That strong, yeah. Also, because it was a bit windy,” she said. “I don’t know if it was coming from the crowd or was from the outside because the wind blows it into the stadium.

“I ‌just hope they are a bit more aware of that stuff,” she added, before laughing when the questions returned to the subject. “Come on, guys. I think there is ‌nothing ‌else to say about weed. I’m just asking people not to smoke it next to the tennis court.”

articles.title: Zeev Buium, Canucks Agree to 8-Year, $75M Contract Extension After Quinn Hughes Trade to Wild
articles.summary: The Vancouver Canucks agreed to an eight-year contract extension worth $75 million with defenseman Zeev Buium, the team announced Friday.
articles.body:
The Vancouver Canucks agreed to an eight-year contract extension worth $75 million with defenseman Zeev Buium, the team announced Friday.

Buium is about to enter his first full season in Vancouver after the team acquired him as part of the blockbuster trade that sent Quinn Hughes to the Minnesota Wild in Dec. 2025. The Canucks also received Marco Rossi, Liam Öhgren and a first-round pick in the deal.

Vancouver eventually selected Adam Novotný with the pick.

Canucks general manager Ryan Johnson was excited about Buium's future with the team following the extension.

"Zeev has settled in nicely with our organization since his trade to Vancouver last season, and we are extremely happy to see him make this long-term commitment to the Canucks," Johnson said as part of Friday's announcement . "He is a key member of our young core and a player we will build around moving forward. Zeev has a lot of upside, and we feel with his abilities he will flourish in the system and environment we are creating inside our locker room. We look forward to working together and creating a strong partnership and foundation for our future."

Buium was initially scheduled to become a restricted free agent following the 2026-27 season before receiving the extension.

The average annual value of $9.38 million on his new deal ranks No. 11 among all defensemen (via Spotrac ).

Buium appeared in 76 combined games with the Canucks and Wild during the 2025-26 season, recording 20 assists and six goals.

Vancouver is attempting to put together a resurgent 2026-27 campaign after coming off a 25-49-8 finish last season.

articles.title: Let the season begin, Hawkeyes open 2026 football season vs Northern Illinois
articles.summary: When date flips to September 5 this weekend, it will have been about 246 days, 5,902 hours, 354,180 minutes, or 21,250,800 seconds since the last Iowa Hawkey...
articles.body:
When date flips to September 5 this weekend, it will have been about 246 days, 5,902 hours, 354,180 minutes, or 21,250,800 seconds since the last Iowa Hawkeye football gameday. Though that was not quite enough time to decide the Hawkeye's quarterback battle between Jeremy Hecklinski and Hank Brown, the expectation to win, a lot, is still on Kirk Ferentz and his Hawkeyes. Ferentz's 28th year as head coach and the 2026 season starts with Northern Illinois on Saturday at 3:15 pm in Kinnick Stadium.

"When football season's here, the world is great," beamed LJ Phillips, a 4th year running back for the Hawkeyes.

While the ultimate goal is to win the first game of the season. The Hawkeyes are hoping to find clarity about their team, specifically at quarterback. All 70,000 people will have their eyes set on Hank Brown or Jeremy Hecklinski, eager to see what they bring to the table. For Hecklinski, he will look to back up his phenomenal Kid's Day performance. For Brown, it will be his first time in a sold out Kinnick Stadium since the loss versus last year's national champion, Indiana.

Players and coaches are adamant that the offense can be successful no matter which quarterback is in.

"The whole identity of the offense is really just the players, it doesn't matter who's in there," said third year Hawkeye tight end DJ Vonnahme. "With either one, we're all tough, we're all being physical."

Nine starters on the offense have been in Tim Lester's system all three years he's been at the helm of the offense. It will be Lester's most experienced team when it comes to understanding the playbook. His Kyle Shanahan style scheme is notably a tough one to learn, but as many have proven from the Shanahan coaching tree, it scores a lot of points. Lester has already nearly doubled the teams' points per game when compared to the season prior to his arrival.

"I definitely feel like this camp definitely had a little more of a jump than the previous camps I was in," said Vonnahme. "So yeah, I think it's just exciting to see how far we can really take this thing."

It's fair to say the playmakers on offense are ready to attack a defense that isn't ran by Iowa defensive coordinator Phil Parker. While the defense is relatively unexperienced, they are primed to continue being one of the best units in the nation, led by cornerback Zach Lutmer and linebacker Jayden Montgomery.

"I got to remind myself that we're going up against a top defense every day," said Phillips. "So sometimes it can be a little frustrating."

Northern Illinois brings in a quarterback battle of their own to the bout in Iowa City. With one little difference. Instead of two guys vying for the job, it's three. Jalon Macon, Taron Dickens and Brady Davidson are all listed on the depth chart separated by the infamous "OR".

"They've got a lot of new players on the roster, and we've got film from all kinds of places trying just to get a feel for personnel," said Ferentz.

He noted it can be a challenge to scout teams who field a roster mainly from the popular transfer portal. In this case, the Hawkeyes can focus on the schemes the Huskies will run. The interim head coach Rob Harley was the Huskies' defensive coordinator last season and the scheme is expected to be the same.

"We're going to attack the scheme that they had last year," said third year wide receiver Tony Diaz. "We just have to see how it goes from there."

The new offensive coordinator for the Huskies is Tony Peterson, a familiar foe.

"We've played against him when he was at Iowa State and Minnesota and now most recently was at Illinois State," said Ferentz. "We know a little bit about the schemes, at least we think we do."

The Hawkeyes played Illinois State in 2024. They won that game 40-0.

"They're going to come in here ready to go, try to upset us and I know they brought in a lot of guys and they're going to come in here and compete, they're going to get after it," said Phillips. "Just excited to go out here, finally play some football."

Tens of thousands of Hawkeye fans feel the same way as Phillips. Hawkeye football is back, finally. The 2026 season kicks off Saturday at 3:15 pm in Kinnick Stadium. Fans that can't make it to the game can watch on Big Ten Network.

articles.title: Branden Sorsby breaks his silence on gambling scandal: ‘Everything can get ripped from you’
articles.summary: Earlier this year, former college quarterback Branden Sorsby was at the center of a high-profile gambling scandal that resulted in his suspension from colleg...
articles.body:
Earlier this year, former college quarterback Branden Sorsby was at the center of a high-profile gambling scandal that resulted in his suspension from college football and the NFL declining to allow him to be picked in the supplemental draft. Now, he's reflecting on the past several months.

While Sorsby released a statement in late June after the NFL declined to hold a supplemental draft, he has not spoken publicly on the scandal. However, in an upcoming four-part Paramount+ documentary focused on Texas Tech called The Program, he has broken his silence.

In the documentary, which was viewed by Justin Williams of The Athletic , Sorsby spoke out on the incident, admitting that he has "a ton of regret" about how everything happened.

"I know how quickly things can go wrong," Sorsby said, via Williams. "Everything can get ripped from you."

In the documentary, Williams says that Sorsby describes going across the Texas border to Oklahoma to legally gamble once he turned 18. He started out playing table games like blackjack, but he eventually got into sports gambling.

That continued even when he was a player at the college level, where Sorsby even bet on his own team while playing for the Indiana Hoosiers.

"I couldn't watch sporting activities without wanting to have something at stake, wanting to have some skin on the game," Sorsby said

Sorsby acknowledged that the habit didn't die once he transferred to Texas Tech, where he was one of the most coveted transfer quarterbacks in the 2026 transfer class, even though he was getting paid quite a lot of money.

"Whenever I got to Tech, same deal. Making more money than I ever made in my life, no reason to gamble. And yet I still did it," Sorsby added. "Just chasing a dopamine hit, and that's where you lose yourself. … I'm walking around the facility and nobody knows that I have a problem gambling. Once I got found out and got caught, I went to rehab to fix my problem. And here we are."

At one point, Sorsby recalled "bawling my eyes out" while on the phone with his parents and agent because he was "thinking I just threw everything I've worked for my entire life out the window."

Sorsby will not be playing football this year, but he will be eligible for the 2027 NFL Draft.

articles.title: Royals vs Blue Jays, September 4 live discussion
articles.summary: Danny Drips arrives on your local TV station
articles.body:
One of the fun things about covering the Friday and Saturday night games all season has been that, on a week like this with one off day, if a good starting pitcher pitches on a Saturday, I get to write about him that night, and I know I'll get to write about him again next Friday. The corollary, however, is that when Daniel "Danny Drips" Lynch IV pitches on a Saturday night, I know I have to write about him the next week.

At first I was fine with the Royals giving him a shot. I wasn't optimistic it would work, but I also didn't think it was going to hurt anything, and it made the guy happy. I'm all for making guys happy. But now that we've seen it for a month or so, it might be making him happy, but it's not making anyone I care about happy. Danny Drips is not a big-league starting pitcher. I remain not-entirely-convinced that he's a big-league reliever. But here he is, starting for the Royals on September 4, while a guy they touted as potentially an answer to their rotation woes for next season pitches for Omaha again. I have a hard time blaming Matt Quatraro and J.J. Picollo for everything that has gone wrong for the Royals this year, but when they do things like this, it gets easier.

Fortunately, the Blue Jays will be countering with Jameson Taillon. Taillon has been a very good starting pitcher for years, but this year his walk rate and home run rates have skyrocketed. That led the Cubs to cut bait on him, despite desperately needing starting pitching as they continue their playoff chase. The Blue Jays picked him up, and he has made two starts totaling eight innings. He's only allowed 3 runs, but he's walked 5 while striking out only 7. It does not feel like he's turned a corner.

What I'm saying is, watch out for dueling no-hitters tonight.

articles.summary: The 2026 NFL season is expected to be Aaron Rodgers' last. The 42-year-old's main goal in retirement will be to start a family with his wife.
articles.body:
Aaron Rodgers is getting ready to play what many are assuming will be his final NFL season after he signed a one-year deal during the offseason to return to the Pittsburgh Steelers .

The 42-year-old quarterback expressed excitement about the chapter of his life that will follow his playing career in a recent interview with Mad Dog Sports Radio's Adam Schein .

In particular, Rodgers is looking forward to starting a family, and expressed hope he and his wife would be in the process of doing so by this time next year.

"I'm hopefully going to be supporting my pregnant wife because we're going to start a family and I am not going to be making a lot of appearances or statements," Rodgers told Schein. "And I'm looking forward to a life of quiet after 22 years in the pros and three in college and getting my body healed up and working on a family. That's what I'm looking forward to."

Revisit Aaron Rodgers' NFL career as he announces 22nd season

Schein sought clarification from Rodgers about whether anything was imminent or if he was simply looking into the proverbial "crystal ball" when assessing his future.

"I'm talking about I'm hoping that I have a pregnant wife by next [year] this time," Rodgers reiterated.

Rodgers also elaborated that his desire to start a family had been spurred, in part, by his recent reconnection with his family , from whom he had previously been estranged.

"I'm definitely excited about it," Rodgers said when addressing the prospect of starting a family. "I mean, being back in my family's lives, I'm having a lot of fun being Uncle Aaron. I have a few godkids that I'm involved with, but being Uncle Aaron to my brother's kids has been a lot of fun."

"And the more I'm around them, the more I get excited, and so does the wife, about having some of our own," he added. "So, I'm excited for that. I can't wait for that next chapter of life and all that that entails, and sleepless nights and crying babies and changing diapers and all those things, I'm looking forward to all of it."

Rodgers has typically kept information about his wife, who he has described as a "private person," close to the vest. As such, it isn't clear whether the 42-year-old quarterback will provide any information if or when they do have a child, especially considering his stated desire to remain out of the public eye following his playing career.

articles.title: Clemson raises contract concerns with LSU over former professional players
articles.summary: Clemson informed LSU that allowing former professional football players to participate in their upcoming game might violate their 2018 agreement, despite rec...
articles.body:
BATON ROUGE, La. ( Louisiana First ) -- Clemson is pointing to its contract with LSU as questions continue over whether former professional football players could take the field for LSU when the two teams meet Saturday.

Yahoo! Sports reported Friday that Clemson officials notified LSU that playing former professional athletes could violate the agreement between the two universities.

An LSU spokesperson confirmed to Louisiana First News that a message circulating publicly from Clemson regarding the agreement was sent to the university.

In the message, Clemson General Counsel W.C. Hood Jr. pointed to a section of the schools' 2018 football agreement that deals with who is eligible to play.

The agreement said player and coach eligibility is determined by NCAA rules, conference rules and each university's rules that are in place on the day of the game.

Hood said Clemson believes that part of the agreement still applies despite the ongoing legal fight over whether former professional athletes can return to college sports.

He wrote that the provision creates a "contractual obligation between the two parties which is not relieved by the ongoing disputes."

"Clemson supports the position of the NCAA and our conferences regarding the eligibility of professional athletes returning to play college football," Hood wrote.

Despite the disagreement, Clemson indicated it is still preparing to play Saturday.

"Our football program and fans are looking forward to visiting your university and the city of Baton Rouge this weekend," Hood wrote.

This comes as LSU, the SEC and several athletes are involved in legal battles over whether former professional players can return to college football.

A Baton Rouge judge granted a preliminary injunction Thursday in favor of student-athletes seeking another year of eligibility, potentially clearing the way for former professional players to join LSU's roster.

Former New Orleans Saints defensive lineman Zxavian Harris and former Cleveland Browns tight end Dae'Quan Wright are among the players hoping to play for LSU.

The SEC has also filed a separate federal lawsuit against LSU over the university's efforts to bring former professional players back to college football.

articles.title: College Football Playoff Reveals Stance on Former NFL Players
articles.summary: College football as a whole is in a state of disarray at the moment. That is because of LSU’s decision to take in players who signed professional contracts a...
articles.body:
College football as a whole is in a state of disarray at the moment. That is because of LSU's decision to take in players who signed professional contracts and spent time in NFL camps this summer.

LSU opens its season against Clemson on Saturday and all eyes will be on Lane Kiffin and whether he plays someone who has left the NFL for LSU. One player in particular, Dae'Quan Wright, already declared he is ready to play.

The SEC has spoken out against such players and now the College Football Playoff committee has shared a take on the matter as well.

College Football Playoff Takes Strong Stance Against LSU

Yahoo Sports insider Ross Dellenger shared the full statement from the CFP.

"The CFP strongly supports the positions and rules of individual conferences concerning the return to college of athletes with professional draft, contract or roster ties," the statement reads. "These conference rules are intended to protect the needs, interests and integrity of the sport. The CFP believes that certain clear rules should be followed so that individual institutions fielding FBS football teams know what will be expected of them, and so that the public can have full confidence in the competitive integrity of the sport. Given the ongoing legal proceedings, we will not have further comments on the matter at this time."

This is a fascinating statement for several reasons. First and foremost, the CFP is taking a clear stance against former pros returning to college football. However, the CFP stops at that and note no more comments will be coming due to all the legal action taking place. Instead, the onus is put on the conferences to deal with the matter, at least for now.

CFP Will Need to Make a Decision Eventually

Leaving this to the conferences for now makes sense as the season is just getting underway. The Playoff itself does not begin for several months. This gives time for the legal process to play out and for conferences to make decisions as well.

But what if former NFL players do play for LSU and it is ruled legal by the courts? That is where the CFP may be stuck, as banning the team could lead to a long, drawn-out legal battle.

The CFP will have to make a decision eventually on whether teams who play former NFL players are eligible for the postseason. The committee is likely hoping the situation is figured out well before the end of the season rolls around.

Lane Kiffin has always been a disruptor and this takes that title to a whole new level. His actions regarding this situation have the potential to change the state of college football as we know it.

articles.title: Serena Williams Aiming To ‘Get Herself Fully Ready’ For Singles In 2027
articles.summary: Serena Williams is using the women’s doubles event at the U.S. Open with her sister Venus in part to prepare herself to return to the singles court in 2027.
articles.body:
Serena Williams is using the women's doubles event at the U.S. Open with her sister Venus in part to prepare herself to return to the singles court in 2027.

"Obviously, Serena and Venus want to win today but for Serena this is also kind of getting ready for the next season, get some points and get movement, play a real match before she really asserts herself back into the singles court," ESPN's Caroline Wozniacki, a close friend of Serena's and a former world No. 1, said on air during the Williams' sisters' doubles match Friday night against Maya Joint and H.C. Chan in Arthur Ashe Stadium.

Asked by Patrick McEnroe if she expects Serena to play singles in 2026 after the U.S. Open, Wozniacki said: "I don't. I think her knee is still not 100%. If it was 100%, I think she would've played singles here so I think she's just gonna go back, get 100% healthy and get herself fully ready for next year."

That timetable would mean a potential return at the Australian Open in January. Williams, 44, has won 23 Grand Slam singles titles, including seven at the Australian Open and six at the U.S. Open.

Appearing Monday on " Good Morning America ," Williams told ESPN's Malika Andrews that she "probably" plans to compete in singles again.

"I probably will play again," she said . "I have to...After some of those returns, I think I need to play at least once."

Williams, who has two young daughters, Olympia and Adira, returned after a four-year layoff to play singles at Wimbledon, losing to Joint in three sets in the first round. She then pulled out of the doubles at Wimbledon with Venus due to a knee injury sustained in singles.

"I injured myself at Wimbledon. And I just didn't have time to recover, unfortunately," Williams said. "And I just didn't want to take any opportunities away from someone if in terms of getting a wild card if I wasn't able to compete at a way that I knew I could."

When Andrews told Williams that many fans hoped to see her compete in a Grand Slam again, Williams replied, "Yeah. I think I will."

"But this isn't something permanent, obviously," she continued. "It's just also really wanting my children to see me play at a different age."

Forbes estimates her net worth at $400 million , making her—by a comfortable margin—the world's richest woman who has made her fortune primarily as an athlete.

The Williams sisters received a wild card to play at the Open and drew tremendous interest, including from Carlos Alcaraz, the defending men's singles champion and Serena's mixed doubles partner at the Open.

"Absolutely," Alcaraz said after his straight-sets win over over Wu Yibing of China. "I mean, I'm gonna get ready. I'm gonna be at the room. I'll be getting treatment with the physio. So I think there is no better plan [than] to watch the doubles, the Williamses, once again, while getting a treatment. I'm going to be ready for that."

articles.title: ESPN picks Detroit Lions' 2026 X-factor
articles.summary: ESPN identified its 2026 X-factor for the Detroit Lions.
articles.body:
Detroit Lions cornerback Rock Ya-Sin was selected by ESPN as the team's biggest X-factor entering the 2026 season.

Detroit released former first-round pick Terrion Arnold back in June, opening the door for Ya-Sin to play opposite D.J. Reed . A second-round selection by the Indianapolis Colts in 2019, Ya-Sin has primarily been a rotational journeyman throughout his NFL career.

National NFL analyst Ben Solak describes Detroit's secondary situation "as dire as there is in the league." Starting safeties Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph will begin the season on the reserve/physically unable to perform list. But, general manager Brad Holmes expressed confidence that both would return at some point this season.

Neither of their replacements served as full-time starters last season, adding another layer of uncertainty to Detroit's revamped secondary. However, Chuck Clark and Avonte Maddox have a combined 170-plus NFL starts between them.

Still, Solak is looking Ya-Sin's direction as the Lions ' defensive X-factor:

The Lions will become the first defense since the 2011 Steelers to start four defensive backs aged 29 or older in Week 1, and only the ninth defense to do it this century. This doesn't disqualify their defensive backfield from playing well, of course -- but it's not like this is their ideal lineup. Clark is a journeyman vet. Maddox was a nickel with the Eagles who flipped to safety only in Detroit. Ya-Sin was supposed to be a backup. The experience of the group might prove a plus, but I'm worried about the collective athleticism. If the Lions struggle for speed and explosive plays in the secondary, DC Kelvin Sheppard will likely pivot to more zone coverages and rely on his rush to win passing downs for him. That's all well and good, but a lack of team speed matters once passes are complete and yards after the catch are available. Also, you will have to play man at some point -- and when you do, Ya-Sin will be targeted. Since he entered the league, Ya-Sin is 12th among all corners in defensive penalties per coverage snap, though he was also ninth in average separation to targeted receivers, according to Next Gen Stats' tracking data and coverage model. He needs to be just as sticky with fewer flags if the Lions' secondary will be competitive. - Ben Solak, ESPN

articles.body:
As the Los Angeles Lakers continue to sift through their offseason points of emphasis, the chatter around Bronny James still hasn't tapered off.

The 21-year-old guard, who is entering his third season, has been a subject of NBA trade rumors since the very moment his father informed the Lakers he wasn't going to return to the franchise to play a ninth season. James' father has been a Philadelphia 76er for nearly two months now, but many continue to wonder if the Jameses are destined to reunite.

A former second round pick, James has a guaranteed contract for the 2026-27 season, which would typically be enough to secure him from all trade speculation for at least one more year. But with the Lakers needing to trim their roster and, quite frankly, with them still needing reinforcements at two major areas on the roster, it isn't surprising to see James mentioned as a potential trade or cut candidate.

Bronny James' Lakers Future: So, What's Up?

L.A. has 16 players on its standard roster, meaning the team needs to drop one player to become compliant with league rules. So, unless the Lakers make a trade, who is poised to be the odd man out?

According to Lakers analyst Trevor Lane, it likely isn't James .

"Could the Lakers move on from Bronny James? He's got a team-option next year, so you would just decline that team-option, you could waive him. That would result in about $2.3 million in dead money sitting in your books. Not the end of the word; that would be just for this season. … That said, Bronny was actually fairly good last season. Quietly, he shot 39 percent from 3, last year Bronny did."

Added Lane: "Will he ultimately become an NBA rotation-level player? We don't know that for sure. I will say that he has improved a ton since he came into the NBA. I wouldn't jump to the conclusion that just because LeBron is no longer a Laker, that Bronny is the guy that's going to get cut. And let's also remember the Lakers did guarantee the half-portion of his salary that was non-guaranteed this summer. So they clearly decided that he is at least worth guaranteeing about half of salary in order to hang on to him.

Lane did acknowledge that while James could get cut, the Lakers have, so far, given many indications that they are prepared to move ahead with the 21-year-old as one of their developing young assets.

The same cannot be said for someone like Dalton Knecht , who entered the NBA with far more expectations than James.

Lane mentioned Jake LaRavia and Jaden Hardy as players who could be on the chopping block but argued that waiving either player wouldn't be in the Lakers' best interest because of their contract situation.

LaRavia and Hardy, both 24, are on expiring $6 million deals, making them potentially attractive salary-fillers in a trade that could deliver the Lakers an impact player.

Meanwhile, as Lane noted, the Lakers have until the end of October to decide if they want to pick up Knecht's team-option. Lane doesn't believe the Lakers will do so, saying it is likely L.A. will end up cutting ties with Knecht, unless the 25-year-old former first round pick particularly excels in preseason and in the first week of the regular season.

articles.title: Chicago Cubs updates: Dansby Swanson progressing with injury — and Javier Assad rejoins team on taxi squad
articles.summary: MIAMI — Dansby Swanson’s unfamiliarity with an oblique strain creates a little uncertainty for the Chicago Cubs shortstop about what his path back might enta...
articles.body:
MIAMI — Dansby Swanson's unfamiliarity with an oblique strain creates a little uncertainty for the Chicago Cubs shortstop about what his path back might entail.

Swanson traveled with the Cubs to Miami for their three-game series against the Marlins that kicked off Friday night at LoanDepot Park. He went through lighter pregame work after having a heavier schedule Thursday. Swanson feels he has been doing a lot to get back on the field as soon as possible, following the guidelines for return to play set by the training staff.

The 32-year-old acknowledged he's not sure where he is at within his rehab progression, which has included fielding grounders and hitting, since he never dealt with an oblique injury before.

"Going into this, the biggest key for me was how to work with a sense of urgency but also with a sense of still being cautious and careful, but not being so cautious and careful that you're not urgent," Swanson said Friday. "They obviously have a good plan. They put together a lot of good things, and I just go at it with my best literally every day and obviously had good results so far and feeling good. Now, what that looks like to get back into like playing, I don't know. We haven't really had those conversations."

Swanson anticipates there will be an adjustment to game speed and pace of play when he does return. Ideally he will have a little bit of a buffer to get back into the flow of the season before the end of September into the playoffs. He has been able to keep his eyes and mind engaged by standing in against a Trajekt Arc pitching machine that can mimic any pitcher's delivery.

"I hate that it happened, and it's obviously like pretty rare for me, but at the end of the day, you can't go back and change it," Swanson said of his injury. "I feel like I've always shown up for my teammates every day when I'm playing, but also there's plenty of ways I can do that now too without playing. So that's something I've enjoyed. And the other day, as bad as I want to be back out there, I can still be present and enjoy this, too, in a way. I know that sounds kind of weird, but just being optimistic and positive is usually a good trait of mine, so just have basically as much fun as I can with it."

Swanson landed on the injured list Aug. 17 and was expected to be out four to six weeks. The Cubs are hoping it'll be the short end of that timeline, which would mean a return before the playoffs. The nature of oblique injuries, which can linger stubbornly, means the Cubs are repeating rehab days with Swanson to make sure he doesn't reaggravate it. They want to get to the point of making sure his oblique can handle full-speed game-level swings and be able to make the awkward moves that sometimes occur, especially on the defensive side.

"There's a difference between feeling it and then still being injured," manager Craig Counsell said. "You have to push through. You have to push some things, and that's just always the balance with these things. This is a muscle that is overused in our sport. You can't avoid it on a daily basis. There's no way we can hide it or stay away from it. You're going to use it every single day, so it's got to be ready to go when you get back into it every day."

As Cubs pitchers gathered in right field for their pregame work Friday, right-hander Javier Assad emerged from the clubhouse to join them.

Assad was on the team's taxi squad for their series opener, but he is expected to factor into their pitching plans this weekend, Counsell said. Assad can be recalled from Triple A as soon as Saturday, the end of the required 15 minimum days spent in the minors after the Cubs optioned him.

As of first pitch Friday night, the Cubs listed their starters for Saturday and Sunday in Miami as to be determined. They could opt to slot Assad into the rotation Saturday and have left-hander Matthew Boyd pitch Sunday's series finale. That would give right-hander Clay Holmes extra rest and line him up to get the ball in Monday's opener in Milwaukee. With an off day Thursday, it would allow the Cubs to reassess if they want to utilize a six-man rotation for another turn or make adjustments to the regular rotation as needed for next weekend's series at Wrigley Field.

Assad has thrived in whatever role the Cubs have asked of the 29-year-old. He has a 2.24 ERA in 64 1/3 innings since the beginning of May.

Right-handers Edward Cabrera and Shelby Miller are continuing to progress in their rehab assignments with Triple-A Iowa as they look to help the Cubs bullpen down the stretch.

Cabrera and Miller were both scheduled to pitch Friday for Iowa, with Cabrera expected to enter the game midinning to help him prepare for his new relief role. If Miller's appearance goes well and the veteran feels good afterward, he is slated to pitch again Saturday for his first back-to-back outings since coming back from his second Tommy John surgery.

Counsell, though, again cautioned about the nature of the rehab process and didn't want to get too far ahead of things in regard to Miller pitching consecutive days, adding, "At some point, we'd definitely want him to go back to back."

Cabrera (blister) allowed one run and struck out two in his first rehab appearance as a reliever Tuesday. He will have additional rehab outings after Friday's, though he likely won't get a chance to pitch back-to-back days with Iowa because of the limited games left in the season.

"We're going to put him through some different scenarios, so to speak," Counsell said. "And we've got a couple more things we'd like to cover."

articles.title: Nothing but praise from Vikings GM on Kevin O'Connell
articles.summary: Nolan Teasley and Kevin O'Connell seem to be working together swimmingly.
articles.body:
Minnesota Vikings general manager Nolan Teasley has had a busy week. The Vikings had to cut down to 53 players on Sunday night, but then made a plethora of notable moves that shook up both the active roster and practice squad over the next two days.

On Wednesday, he met with the media following the roster overhaul. He answered questions about J.J. McCarthy and new free-agent addition Kyle Van Noy.

Teasley was also asked what he had learned about Kevin O'Connell since being hired in early June. The general manager, who has a history with O'Connell, heaped praise upon the coach.

[O'Connell is] highly intelligent, a great football mind, a big-picture thinker as a head coach, which I think is really important," Teasley answered . "And it's just been really seamless and really easy for us to stay on the same page and communicate daily about every aspect of our football operation.

"I'm really happy with where that relationship is and excited to continue to work with him."

This is a pivotal year for O'Connell, who has gone 43-25 in four seasons but has yet to win a playoff game. The hope is that Teasley can build a stronger roster than Kwesi Adofo-Mensah, who served as GM during the first four years of O'Connell's tenure.

articles.title: 49ers are facing adversity before season even begins
articles.summary: The 49ers have a December injury report in September
articles.body:
While not the opening game, the Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers will help kickoff the season on Thursday night in Melbourne, Australia.

The 49ers are far from at full force. They are facing significant attrition and adversity before the new year even begins.

Nick Bosa's backups, Sam Okuayinonu and rookie Romello Height , did not make the international trip. Bosa himself is recovering from last year's ACL injury and tendinitis. Bosa himself will probably play . The bigger question is whether the star pass rusher will handle a full workload and/or look like himself.

George Kittle—one of the best tight ends in football—tore his Achilles tendon in January. He's trending in the direction of playing , but it's difficult to imagine he'll have a full workload. With a limited receiver corps, that we will get to in a second, not having Kittle at his best is a significant roadblock for the San Francisco offense.

And then there are the receivers. Ricky Pearsall—someone the team expected to take a significant jump in year three—was shut down for the year. Christian Kirk, added in free agency as a footnote to their splash signing of Mike Evans, will start the season on injured reserve and miss at least the first four games. Evans missed most of training camp with an abductor, groin, quad injury and may also be on a limited pitch count similar to Bosa and Kittle.

That leaves San Francisco with rookie De'Zhaun Stribling—the betting favorite to lead this year's draft class in receiving yards—Deebo Samuel, Demarcus Robinson, Jordan Watkins, and Jacob Cowing to catch passes from Brock Purdy. That list won't exactly have a reloaded Rams secondary shaking in their boots, especially if Evans is limited or unavailable.

Last year's overdrafted EDGE defender Mykel Williams will miss at least the first four games on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list. Safety Malik Mustapha is trending out of the Week 1 opener. Starting guard Dominick Puni suffered a concussion in camp and may not be ready in time.

And all of this before we even mention Kyle Shanahan's offseason adversity and the fact he might not be 100% at this point either.

And, on top of that, have I mentioned that the 49ers will line up against Myles Garrett, Aaron Donald, and Trent McDuffie?

While the 49ers have a strong track record of winning under Shanahan, this seems to be a season where they at best finish in the middle of the pack. Their core has aged significantly and they were already players who were no strangers to injury.

It's hard to imagine San Francisco keeping Thursday's game competitive. It's even more difficult to think they can stave off the injury bug long enough to maintain a position in the playoff picture towards the end fo the year.

The 49ers' season may be over before it even begins.

After the Washington Huskies dipped into Texas to land a commitment from four-star wide receiver Tre Moore in the 2027 class, Jedd Fisch and position coach Kevin Cummings are looking to repeat that in 2028 with four-star Carter St. Junious .

St. Junious, a 6-foot-3, 185-pound product of Manvel High School, is ranked as the nation's No. 145 overall prospect and No. 22 wide receiver in the 2028 class by the 247Sports Composite, and has become one of the most-coveted underclassmen in the country.

St. Junious has accrued 40 offers, with LSU, Nebraska, Oregon, Texas, Texas Tech, and many other Power Four programs in the hunt for his services. However, the Huskies have put themselves in a strong position early on in his recruitment.

"Washington is definitely a program that excites me," St. Junious told Rivals' Steve Wiltfong (subscription required) . "I like what Coach Fisch is building and the way their offense gives receivers opportunities to make plays. They have a great tradition and compete at a high level. I'm looking forward to continuing to build that relationship and learning more about the program."

After posting 40 catches for 585 yards and 5 touchdowns during his sophomore season, St. Junious is off to a promising start in his junior year, hauling in 7 receptions for 140 yards and a pair of touchdowns during his season debut. In his dominant season opener, he showcased his long speed, ability to thrive in contested catches, and route-running prowess, which could help him make an early impact at the college level.

With four freshmen on the roster in 2026 and four more receivers committed to the 2027 class, Fisch and Cummings can be somewhat selective at the position in 2028, as St. Junious appears to be among their top priorities.

articles.title: Geno Auriemma: ‘College sports is dying’
articles.summary: Millions of fans are preparing to watch and attend Week 1 of the college football season, but Geno Auriemma says the empire is dying. Auriemma is forecasting...
articles.body:
Millions of fans are preparing to watch and attend Week 1 of the college football season, but Geno Auriemma says the empire is dying.

Auriemma is forecasting the death of college sports as Lane Kiffin prepares for his first game as head coach of LSU by continuing his push to bring a former NFL player back to college. The iconic UConn women's basketball head coach made the prediction with Yahoo Sports Daily hosts Caroline Fenton and Jason Fitz.

"College sports is dying," Auriemma said. "And you know, I've had parents pass away. And when they were dying on the inside, they didn't always show it on the outside. On the outside, sometimes it looks like, 'Wow, everything's great.'"

This weekend will be one of those times where everything looks great. The college basketball tournament is similarly one of those times where everything always looks great. Fans, analysts, and media can spend the offseason forecasting the death of college sports , but once the biggest games are played, all is well again.

"On the inside it's dying," Auriemma said before getting more graphic. "Because every single day, something comes up to show you a symptom of the disease that we're suffering."

Auriemma insisted he's not saying student athletes shouldn't be paid or have the right to enter the transfer portal, but he did say fans should be able to follow the sports they love without seeing constant lawsuits, legal battles, and bickering amongst coaches and schools trying to gain an edge or alter the system.

"The more this happens, and the more these things keep being the central focus of the news, the more we're dying one day at a time," he continued. "And until somebody comes along and says, 'This is it, these are the rules, and that's it.'"

It's fair to question whether the constant fear-mongering around NIL and the transfer portal, which spells doom, is healthy for college sports. But it's hard to imagine what the last few years of media coverage of college basketball and football would have been like without NIL and transfer portal discussions.

They've added controversy to college sports, sure. But with powerhouse teams and brands, the top-heavy nature of college basketball and football is also keeping them as relevant as they've ever been. There's a reason ESPN is talking less baseball and more college football than ever. And it's not because college sports is dying.

articles.title: Magnus Carlsen, Anish Giri, Vidit Gujrathi, Divya Deshmukh, Koneru Humpy in one team: How GCL made it possible
articles.summary: Chess News: Magnus Carlsen, Anish Giri, Vidit Gujrathi, Koneru Humpy, Divya Deshmukh, Volodar Murzin. Wait. This isn’t a draft for an all-star exhibition tourname.
articles.body: Magnus Carlsen, Anish Giri, Vidit Gujrathi, Koneru Humpy, Divya Deshmukh, Volodar Murzin. Wait. This isn’t a draft for an all-star exhibition tournament, but the six-member roster that the Alpine APL Pipers have assembled to defend their Global Chess League (GCL) crown for Season 4 in Bengaluru.If last season was about breaking the stranglehold of the Triveni Continental Kings to lift their maiden title, Season 4, starting this Saturday, is likely to be about something far more terrifying for the rest of the field.Pairing World No. 1 Magnus Carlsen alongside positional titans Anish and Vidit, backed by the veteran grit of Humpy, FIDE Women's World Cup winner Divya, and former World Rapid Champion Murzin on the prodigy board, the Pipers have crafted what might be the most formidable franchise lineup ever placed on the battlefield of 64 squares.But how do you assemble a modern-day Dream Team under a strict draft system where every single team enters the bidding room with identical resources?How can someone build a team like that?Pipers' coach Pravin Thipsay believes that constructing a squad of this calibre isn't about collecting shiny names."It's not a sort of building a star-studded lineup," Thipsay told TimesofIndia.com during an exclusive interaction, dismissing the notion that the roster came together by accident."It's important to have strong players since it's a double round-robin for qualification to the top two spots, and then it's going to be a one-to-one match. So there are two phases. We should have a team which is very good at beating some of the teams so that we finish in the top two, and in the second phase, once we end up in the top two, it's important to beat the other teams."In a franchise ecosystem, every team starts with an identical bank of draft points.Securing an Icon board like Magnus Carlsen, who returns to lead the Pipers after skipping last season, requires an immediate, massive financial outlay. The moment you go big on the top board, your remaining purse is instantly squeezed, forcing coaches into high-wire balancing acts for the Superstar and Prodigy boards.“The best parameter in judging strength or the present strength of a player is the Elo rating, and that's the reason why I personally try to have the strongest rated players in my team,” Thipsay admitted.“Now, the process of the draft is quite clear, and everybody starts with an equal number of points. How you spend those points in selecting the players, that is important.”In reality, every coach walks into the venue eyeing the exact same elite names on each tier.“Very often you have to spend most of your points on one or two players, and that leaves you in a tricky situation where you have lesser points, and you may not always get the best player you want,” the 67-year-old veteran Grandmaster added. “Nobody gets all the six players of their choice because others also aim for those players. So somewhere you have to see the balance. If you are able to get three of the most wanted or most coveted players in your team, I think it's a good team to start with. It's a tricky procedure to outmanoeuvre the other coaches. It's much trickier than what it appears to be.”By securing Giri and Vidit to flank Carlsen on the top boards, while locking in Humpy, Divya Deshmukh, and Murzin, who offers incredible fast-chess firepower as a former World Rapid Champion, the Pipers managed to pull off the ultimate draft sweep across every single board category.Behind the champion’s burdenCarrying the title of defending champions only heightens the target on their backs. Coach Thipsay knows that pretty well.“The most important thing is, as defending champions, we should not be overconfident,” Thipsay told this website with some palpable firmness. “And we should not be again very attentive to the media. As a defending champion, the media is going to approach us more frequently than the other teams. But the most important factor in the game of chess is your preparation, your practice, your rest on that day.”To combat the attention that inevitably surrounds a squad featuring Carlsen, Giri, and rising elite talents, Thipsay has already mapped out a strict operational barrier for the tournament.“We are going to see that at no stage our players are losing their focus due to the media attention or anything else. So I am going to restrict the promotional activities to short tenures, very often after the games,” he revealed.The prep of defending championsOver the last few weeks, Thipsay has put his efforts into focusing heavily on the current form of his players rather than relying on their classical reputations.“It's important to prepare once we know who is playing whom,” Thipsay acknowledged. “The board order was disclosed, so we started personally preparing against those opponents. The Icon board would prepare against all the Icons, and so on. I personally look at the games of these players and shortcomings in their recent games. I focus on finding out shortcomings of the opponents in their recent rapid games, not the classical ones. So that is my strategy.”Is nothing going to stop Pipers then?With the preliminary double round-robin kicking off at The Lalit Ashok Bangalore, the major challenge for the Pipers is perhaps more of a psychological nature. The underdog plays with uninhibited freedom, while the favourite carries the weight of the result."It's general public psychology and, of course, player psychology that opponents do better against the defending champions or against a stronger team," Thipsay reflected."The opposition which we are going to face could be more fierce, more prepared, and more motivated when playing with us, simply because there is an opportunity to beat the defending champions.”Mitigating that threat for Thipsay means continuously reminding his superstar roster that past titles and Elo ratings offer zero safety once the clock starts ticking.“We have to take into account that the same opponents may not be so strong against other teams, but they could be strong against our team,” he warned. “The second challenge I see is that the fact that we won in the third season doesn't mean that we're going to win the fourth season. Our team will have to be careful about any overconfidence that comes from results in preliminaries or earlier tournaments. Every game is a different one, and how you played yesterday has no bearing over how you are going to play today.”ALSO SEE: All the squads of GCL 2026 teamsAs the clock ticks down to Round 1 in Bengaluru, the Alpine APL Pipers stand on the precipice of GCL history. On paper, they have constructed a masterpiece. On the board, the hard work begins all over again.“At the moment, we are well poised,” Thipsay concluded with trademark calmness. “The immediate goal is simple: finish in the top two in the preliminaries. Because after the preliminaries, there is no option. You have to try to be the champion.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Gukesh's lifetime dream just came too early': American GM Levon Aronian assesses Sindarov clash | Exclusive

articles.body: World Championship challenger Javokhir Sindarov is not thinking about the summit clash against Dommaraju Gukesh yet.Earlier this year, the 20-year-old Uzbek earned his shot at the title by winning the Cyprus Candidates with a round to spare. But having returned to the country where it all began — it was in India that Sindarov won the FIDE World Cup in Goa in 2025 to qualify for the Candidates — he is keen to talk about everything except the upcoming Geneva encounter, where he will take on Gukesh in a series of 14 classical games running from November 22 to December 13."Right now, I'm focusing on my next events: the Global Chess League and the Olympiad," he told reporters on Friday. "After those, I will start preparing for the World Championship match."The Global Chess League (GCL) begins on Saturday. The Uzbek Grandmaster plays for the American Gambits there, then turns out for his national team at the Olympiad in Samarkand from 15 to 27 September.Gukesh will also represent India at the Chess Olympiad, but the GCL is one of several tournaments he has chosen to skip as he sharpens his focus on the World Championship match.American Grandmaster Levon Aronian senses that the title fight between two 20-year-olds will hinge as much on temperament as on preparation."Gukesh is a big fighter," he told TimesofIndia.com during an exclusive interview. "He has been a bit down, but I expect him to be in a fighting mood for the match. Of course, it's a tremendous pressure."Gukesh became world champion at 18, the youngest to do so. Aronian sees an echo of an earlier era in that. Mikhail Tal, who won the title at 23 in 1960, was himself the youngest world champion of his time, before Garry Kasparov broke the record 25 years later."You know, you're so young and your lifetime dream just came too early. I think the same kind of thing happened to Mikhail Tal. He also became a world champion too early. And of course, it's normal to be overwhelmed," Aronian added.From a strategic point of view, Aronian feels the wider chess world to have already made up its mind about how Gukesh will approach the match."I think people at the moment, they think that Gukesh is going to go and try to be very cautious, like in the similar style, like Ding (Liren) was doing against Nepomniachtchi, or also the way Ding was playing against Gukesh as well," he said with a smile.Whether that script holds against Sindarov, he added, is the interesting question."There are so many choices to make, and it's definitely going to be an interesting match from a strategical point. I expect Sindarov to be continuing playing very interesting chess the way he's doing. It's an interesting clash, I think. Hopefully, there will be lots of resulting games," he opined.Asked whether failing to win the World Championship title himself was a source of regret, Aronian, who has been ranked World No. 2 and has won world titles in every format except classical, concluded, "I have no regrets whatsoever, because I never valued myself so highly as a chess player. Of course, I have talent, and I'm better than many of the world champions in my understanding of chess. But the way I got to be number two is already a miracle for me; my knowledge of chess was so much worse before.ALSO READ: 'I'm Surprised': Levon Aronian on weakness Praggnanandhaa fixed to win India's historic GCT title | Exclusive"I'm not sure that setting up goals is a good thing for you. Sometimes it just adds to the anxiety. I think it's better just to enjoy and cherish what you have."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Lakers Trade Pitch Lands Brook Lopez, Clippers Wing Amid Kawhi Leonard Drama
articles.summary: An intriguing Lakers trade idea doing the rounds would let the franchise reunite with Brook Lopez and add Derrick Jones Jr. from the Clippers. The post Laker...
articles.body:
The LA Clippers are in disarray after the NBA stripped them of five future first-round picks for circumventing the salary cap to benefit Kawhi Leonard. With the Clippers pivoting toward a rebuild under Keaton Wagler, the Lakers have a prime opportunity to poach displaced veterans from their cross-town rival.

One intriguing Lakers trade idea doing the rounds would let the franchise reunite with Brook Lopez, their starting center during the 2017-18 season, and add Derrick Jones Jr., who played alongside Luka Doncic during the 2024 NBA Finals.

Lakers would receive: Brook Lopez, Derrick Jones Jr.

Clippers would receive: Jaden Hardy, Jake LaRavia, Dalton Knecht

Both Lopez and Jones are defensive-minded players, which bodes well for the new-look Lakers roster that leans heavily toward offense.

Relying solely on Walker Kessler and Kevon Looney to anchor the Lakers' center rotation next season is a massive gamble. Last year, the duo combined for just 26 appearances: Kessler lost nearly his entire season to shoulder surgery in Utah, while Looney battled injuries and fell out of James Borrego's interim rotation. Banking on two injury-prone bigs is a dangerous proposition in a Western Conference featuring Victor Wembanyama and Nikola Jokic.

Brook Lopez has been very healthy even this late into his career, having played 75, 80, 79 and 78 games in his last four seasons with the Clippers and Milwaukee Bucks . The 38-year-old is still an elite rim protector who can step away from the hoop and make threes, giving JJ Redick a reliable backup center and a proper stretch-5 to call upon. In fact, Lopez also has the versatility of playing next to Kessler in certain lineups.

As for Jones, the proof is in the pudding. The athletic wing started all 22 games during the Mavericks ' run to the 2024 NBA Finals, averaging 9.1 points and 3.1 rebounds while shooting a reliable 37% from three. He also played excellent defense in those playoffs. His proven chemistry with Luka Doncic makes him an attractive piece to the Lakers.

The best part? Both Lopez ($9.1M) and Jones ($10.4M) are on expiring contracts, making it a very risk-free Lakers trade proposition.

Lopez and Jones are veterans who deserve to play on playoff teams at this stage of their careers. The Clippers, after trading Kawhi Leonard to the Toronto Raptors , are projected to finish in the bottom half of the West next season.

Taking a chance on a young prospect like Dalton Knecht makes complete sense for the Clippers, as it aligns with the timeline of their core centered around Keaton Wagler. Meanwhile, veterans like Hady and Jake LaRavia are on expiring deals, giving Los Angeles the flexibility to simply let them walk or cut ties in a year.

articles.title: Yankees’ Provide Critical Update On Ryan Weathers
articles.summary: Yankees left-handed starting pitcher Ryan Weathers is reportedly “expected to begin his throwing program this weekend,” according to Yankees Manager Aaron Bo...
articles.body:
Yankees left-handed starting pitcher Ryan Weathers is reportedly "expected to begin his throwing program this weekend," according to Yankees Manager Aaron Boone and reported by Yankees beat writer Chris Kirschner of The Athletic. Weathers, who's 26 years old, has posted an impressive first season in pinstripes with the Yankees after being traded there over the offseason from the Miami Marlins. In 25 games, Weathers has posted a 5-8 record with a 3.60 ERA and 143 strikeouts over 137.1 innings. Weathers was placed on the 15-day injured list back on August 23rd due to a left forearm flexor strain, which had him removed in the middle of a start on Saturday, August 22nd, versus the Toronto Blue Jays at Yankee Stadium in the top of the 4th.

Weathers Having Strong First Season In New York

Weathers was especially dominant in his previous seven starts, where he posted a 2.27 ERA with 33 strikeouts in 39.2 innings pitched and a 1.18 WHIP. Weathers has never thrown more than 100 innings in a big league season until this year with the Yankees, in which he's so far at 137.1 innings, which surpasses his previous career high of 94.1 innings back in 2021 as a rookie with the San Diego Padres. There's no denying the clear arm talent with Weathers; the problem has been staying healthy over the course of a full big-league season. Weathers injury history is real. Weathers suffered from lat and forearm injuries last year. He then had finger, ankle, and arm-related injuries spanning from 2021-24.

This has led to Weathers bouncing between starting pitcher and reliever in the majors. But this has arguably been Weathers best season up to date, performance-wise and health-wise. The Yankees needed Weathers to step up in the rotation due to injuries to Max Fried and the recovery of Gerrit Cole from Tommy John Surgery, and Weathers stepped up as the middle rotation arm in such capacity.

Yankees Have Important Decision To Make With Weathers

However, factoring in long-term health down the stretch and for an inevitable October playoff push at this point, it's up for questioning whether the Yankees decide to transition Weathers into a high-leverage bullpen role at some point or not as we get closer to the postseason. With just 20 games remaining and the Yankees three games back of the Tampa Bay Rays from first place in the AL East, the playoff format conversation becomes even more of an interesting topic. It's also left in question how long it will take Weathers to ramp up before an eventual return.

Weathers has been efficient with inducing ground balls this year as well, with a 49.5 ground ball percentage, placing him in the 83rd percentile, according to Baseball Savant. The Yankees have several questions to answer regarding their pitching down the stretch and in the postseason, with Clarke Schmidt rehabbing in Triple-A and transitioning to a bullpen role , along with the return of Luis Gil to the Yankees bullpen, who originally came up as a starter in 2024.

These conversations will certainly be interesting and possibly rather difficult for Yankees brass as we approach the final stretch of the 2026 regular season in September, with October looming. Whether the Yankees continue to use Weathers out of the rotation or transitioning him into a bullpen role for October is something to keep an eye on within the next several upcoming weeks.

articles.title: ‘The Eventual Target Could Be Bill Belichick’ — Insider Reveals How North Carolina Could Try to Cut Ties With $50M HC Amid Investigation
articles.summary: The most important document in Chapel Hill right now could very well be Article 11 of Bill Belichick’s contract. North Carolina’s widening inquiry into its f...
articles.body:
The most important document in Chapel Hill right now could very well be Article 11 of Bill Belichick's contract.

North Carolina's widening inquiry into its football program has already coincided with general manager Michael Lombardi's resignation and questions surrounding defensive coordinator Steve Belichick.

Mike Florio believes the same inquiry could eventually reach the head coach, and any evidence that gives UNC valid cause to terminate him could carry tens of millions of dollars in financial consequences.

Mike Florio Flags Contract Pressure Point That Could Hurt Bill Belichick

"The eventual target could be coach Bill Belichick," Florio wrote in his NBC Sports analysis .

That possibility revolves around language buried inside Belichick's five-year, $50 million agreement.

Contract language in Article 11(c) gives UNC a path to terminate him for cause in certain situations involving conduct by Belichick or people he supervises, including conduct "known by Coach" and not properly reported when it ultimately leads to a material disciplinary finding, action, or sanction.

WRAL reported that lawyers conducting the investigation asked interviewees whether they had reported potentially questionable behavior to Belichick.

Investigators have also asked questions about whether Steve Belichick used drugs on the job or provided drugs to a player, along with separate allegations involving possible sexual relationships between staff members and players or other staffers.

WRAL has not reported that Belichick knew about any alleged misconduct, failed to report it, or violated university policy.

PREDICT THE CFB SEASON: PFN's Free CFB Playoff Predictor

Florio nevertheless sees the contract language as a possible pressure point if the investigation eventually produces evidence connecting Belichick to a reporting failure.

He also wrote that someone inside UNC "may be looking for a reason to fire Belichick for cause."

A For-Cause Firing Would Change the Money

UNC guaranteed the first three years of Belichick's $50 million contract. WRAL reported that if the university dismissed him without cause, it would owe the compensation scheduled through Dec. 31, 2027.

For cause is a different financial lane. Belichick's agreement says UNC would not owe salary, bonuses or supplemental income after a valid termination for cause, creating an obvious financial distinction if university leadership ever decided the relationship had run its course.

There is no reporting that UNC has made that decision. Hence, Florio's piece is merely an interpretation of where the investigation could lead, and not evidence that administrators have chosen Belichick as their next target.

Not to mention, the timing makes the split-screen around the program especially strange. North Carolina opened Belichick's second season with a 15-10 win over TCU, holding the Horned Frogs scoreless for the final 49 minutes.

PFN currently gives the Tar Heels an 89.1 Defense Impact score, good enough for No. 2 nationally.

One side of Chapel Hill is finally producing the result Belichick was hired to deliver. The other is reading contracts, interviewing witnesses, and asking questions that could become much more expensive than anything happening on Saturdays.
