articles.title: Iván Herrera's 3-run homer in the 9th inning rallies the Cardinals to a 7-6 win over the Rockies
articles.summary: Iván Herrera hit a three-run homer in the ninth inning to rally the St. Louis Cardinals past the Colorado Rockies 7-6 on Friday night, tightening a crowded r...
articles.body:
DENVER (AP) — Iván Herrera hit a three-run homer in the ninth inning to rally the St. Louis Cardinals past the Colorado Rockies 7-6 on Friday night, tightening a crowded race for the final National League wild card.

St. Louis pulled even with Miami at 71-71 as both teams chase San Diego (74-67) and Arizona (74-68) for the last NL playoff berth.

With the Cardinals trailing 6-4 in the ninth, Thomas Saggese drew a leadoff walk from Jordan Romano (0-3) and stole second with one out. He went to third when José Fermín reached on a throwing error by third baseman Connor Norby.

Herrera then drove a 1-2 slider 430 feet to center field for his 15th home run, handing Romano his fourth blown save.

Riley O'Brien struck out two in the ninth for his 36th save. After committing a throwing error on a pickoff attempt that advanced the potential tying run to second base, O'Brien fanned rookie Cole Carrigg to end it.

Cade Winquist (1-0) worked 1 2/3 scoreless innings for his first major league win.

Carrigg hit an inside-the-park home run and TJ Rumfield also homered and finished with three hits for Colorado.

The Rockies rallied to take the lead in the sixth after St. Louis starter Andre Pallante held them to a run through five innings.

Rumfield hit a one-out triple off Hancel Rincon, who was making his major league debut, and scored on a wild pitch. Carrigg's drive off the wall in center got away from outfielder Nathan Church, and the speedy Carrigg scored easily.

Justin Bruihl, who came on after a single, was called for a pitch-clock violation. Cardinals manager Oliver Marmol argued with plate umpire Doug Eddings and was ejected.

Norby scored on Adael Amador's single, and Troy Johnston was ruled safe when he raced home from third on Zac Veen's sacrifice bunt. Replays showed catcher Leo Bernal tagged Johnston, but St. Louis lost its challenge earlier in the inning on Rumfield's triple.

Rumfield's solo homer in the seventh, his 15th of the season, extended the lead.

Cardinals LHP Matthew Liberatore (5-13, 5.41 ERA) goes for his first win in nine starts against Rockies rookie RHP Mason Adams (0-0, 3.00) on Saturday night.

articles.title: Rockies rally, then watch it disappear in 7-6 loss to Cardinals
articles.summary: Colorado erased a three-run deficit with a four-run sixth inning, but Iván Herrera’s three-run homer off Jordan Romano flipped the game again in the ninth.
articles.body:
The Rockies spent much of Friday night letting opportunities slip away, then finally broke through in a four-run sixth inning that turned a 4-1 deficit into a 5-4 lead.

TJ Rumfield added insurance with a 441-foot home run an inning later, and the bullpen carried the two-run advantage into the ninth.

Jordan Romano opened the ninth with a walk, Connor Norby made a throwing error and Iván Herrera crushed a three-run homer to center as the Cardinals came back for a 7-6 win at Coors Field.

Colorado fell to 54-87, while St. Louis improved to 71-71. Cade Winquest earned the win to improve to 1-0, Romano took the loss and fell to 0-3, and Riley O'Brien recorded his 36th save.

Ryan Feltner's final line was uneven, but there were stretches where his stuff looked quite good.

The right-hander allowed four runs on seven hits and three walks over five innings, striking out five while throwing 62 of his 95 pitches for strikes.

All five of Feltner's strikeouts came on the changeup, which generated three whiffs on seven swings.

He looked sharp immediately, retiring the Cardinals in order in the first and finishing Iván Herrera with an 84.4 mph changeup for a swinging strikeout.

The second inning was much more difficult.

Jordan Walker opened with a single and Leo Bernal walked before Nolan Gorman tied the game with an RBI single. Thomas Saggese then won a seven-pitch battle with Feltner and doubled home Joshua Báez to put St. Louis ahead 2-1.

Feltner responded with an excellent third, needing just nine pitches to retire Herrera, Alec Burleson and Walker in order. Burleson chased a changeup below the zone for strike three, while Walker took another one to end the inning.

A leadoff walk to Bernal created more traffic in the fourth, but Feltner retired the next three hitters.

Nathan Church opened with a soft single, Bryan Torres walked and Herrera reached on a 104.2 mph grounder to short. Burleson followed with a high chopper that Carrigg charged, but the ball kicked off the heel of his glove as a runner crossed in front of him. It was scored an RBI single.

The Rockies did make one excellent defensive play in the middle of the inning.

Walker lifted a relatively shallow fly to center, where Jake McCarthy caught it moving toward the infield and made a strong throw toward home. TJ Rumfield cut the throw off after the run scored and helped catch Herrera between second and third for a double play.

Bernal then doubled at 109.8 mph, although McCarthy made a sliding stop in deep right-center that kept the ball from reaching the wall and prevented another run from scoring in that moment.

Feltner eventually got Báez to end the inning.

His four-seamer still averaged 94.4 mph and touched 96.6, while the changeup gave him a legitimate finishing pitch. The command was not consistent enough to keep St. Louis from creating traffic.

The Rockies scored before recording a hit.

McCarthy opened the bottom of the first with a four-pitch walk, stole second, moved to third on Mickey Moniak's groundout and scored on Hunter Goodman's sacrifice fly.

Colorado had chances for much more against Andre Pallante.

Carrigg opened the second with a triple and never moved the final 90 feet. Norby grounded out, Troy Johnston walked, Adael Amador sacrificed Johnston to second and Zac Veen grounded out to end the inning.

Goodman and Rumfield then drew consecutive two-out walks in the third before Carrigg grounded out on the first pitch he saw.

Norby singled to begin the fourth, but Johnston grounded into a double play. Pallante then worked a clean fifth to finish five innings with only one run allowed on two hits and four walks.

He struck out just one and generated only four whiffs on 33 swings, but Colorado did almost nothing with the contact it made. The Rockies averaged just 74.4 mph on 15 balls in play against him.

Pallante had retired seven straight and had thrown only 72 pitches through five.

Hancel Rincon entered for his major-league debut and got Goodman to line out.

Rumfield drove a ball into right and raced into third. St. Louis challenged the safe call, but replay upheld it.

Rincon then threw a wild pitch that brought Rumfield home.

Carrigg followed by driving a ball into the right-center gap and never stopped running, coming all the way around for an inside-the-park home run to cut the deficit to 4-3.

Norby singled, and that ended Rincon's debut after just one-third of an inning.

Justin Bruihl replaced him, but Cardinals manager Oliver Marmol was still arguing with the umpires as the pitching change was made. The argument continued before play resumed, and Marmol kept yelling from the dugout until home-plate umpire Doug Eddings ejected him.

Once play resumed, Johnston doubled Norby to third and Amador tied the game with an RBI single to right.

He missed his first attempt at a safety squeeze before getting the second bunt down toward the third-base side of the mound. Bruihl charged and shoveled the ball home with his glove, but Johnston was ruled safe.

The Cardinals had already used their replay challenge on Rumfield's triple and could not challenge the play at the plate.

Colorado had turned a 4-1 deficit into a 5-4 lead.

Mark Manfredi gave the Rockies exactly what they needed after Feltner.

The left-hander retired all six hitters he faced over two perfect innings and struck out two.

His fastball averaged 95 mph, nearly a full mile per hour above his season average, while his slider generated two whiffs on four swings.

With two outs, Carrigg ranged toward the middle on Church's grounder, charged it, fielded it on the backhand and fired a strong throw to first that narrowly beat the runner.

Manfredi came back for the seventh and retired another three in order, ending his night by winning an eight-pitch battle with Burleson on a 94 mph fastball.

Then Rumfield gave the Rockies some breathing room.

Goodman drove a ball 382 feet to center but came up just short.

He got a 2-0 sweeper and launched it 441 feet to right-center for his 15th home run, extending the lead to 6-4.

Jimmy Herget took over in the eighth and retired Walker and Bernal before Báez singled with two outs. Brennan Bernardino then came on to retire pinch-hitter Ramón Urías and preserve the two-run lead.

Colorado managed only a two-out infield single from Ezequiel Tovar in the bottom half.

Romano opened the ninth with a seven-pitch walk to Saggese.

Church flew out, but Saggese stole second before José Fermín hit a slow ground ball toward third. Norby's throw got away, putting runners at second and third with one out.

Romano left an 84.2 mph slider over the plate, and Herrera drove it 430 feet to center at 103.5 mph.

Romano retired only one hitter, allowing three runs — two earned — on one hit and one walk.

O'Brien opened the bottom of the ninth with three straight sweepers to Moniak.

Goodman grounded out before Rumfield singled with two outs and Ryan Ritter entered to run for him. O'Brien then threw away a pickoff attempt, moving the tying run into scoring position.

O'Brien threw him three straight sweepers.

The Rockies spent the early innings creating opportunities without finishing them.

Carrigg's leadoff triple went to waste in the second. Consecutive two-out walks produced nothing in the third. Colorado finished just 1-for-8 with runners in scoring position and left eight runners on base.

Rumfield finished 3-for-4 with a triple, homer and two runs scored. Carrigg went 2-for-5 with a triple and an inside-the-park homer.

The defense had its moments too. McCarthy made multiple important plays in center, Amador made a slick backhand play up the middle and Carrigg made a strong play to finish Manfredi's first inning.

Manfredi was excellent, and Herget and Bernardino kept the lead intact through the eighth.

The Rockies did enough to erase a three-run deficit and build a two-run lead.

The Rockies and Cardinals continue their series Saturday night at Coors Field, with first pitch scheduled for 6:10 p.m. MDT .

Colorado will send Mason Adams to the mound for the third start of his major-league career. The right-hander enters 0-0 with a 3.00 ERA and 10 strikeouts .

St. Louis will counter with left-hander Matthew Liberatore , who enters 5-13 with a 5.41 ERA and 141 strikeouts .

articles.title: Totino-Grace football's rushing attack wears down No. 13 Rocori in Week 1 upset
articles.summary: No. 13 Rocori came into the season with a new coach and high hopes, but Totino-Grace and running back Fua Taumalolo had other plans.
articles.body:
COLD SPRING — Coming out of halftime, the Totino-Grace football team held firm with a six-point lead and possession to start the third quarter.

The Eagles had been playing well, pounding the rock against a strong Rocori defense and getting scores from both running backs, sophomore Fua Taumalolo and senior Ben Bergan.

Yet it was an eight-minute, 41-yard scoreless drive that ultimately sealed the win against No. 13 Rocori.

After finally getting their defense off the field, the Spartans quickly gave the ball right back to the Eagles. They swiftly marched down the field to punch in the insurance score of a 20-8 victory.

Totino-Grace had possession for 11 of the 12 minutes in the third quarter.

"We have got to execute," first-year Rocori head coach Alex Larson said. "We're putting our guys in position; I think we just got to do a better job of when we get that opportunity to execute on it."

All night long the Eagles' rushing attacked worked effortlessly and effectively, that elusive drive still being the pinnacle of effective game prep and scouting over a Rocori squad that has high expectations in 2026.

The biggest factor to that success was, of course, the offensive line paving the way for both Taumalolo and Bergan.

"They played really well," Taumalolo said. "I feel like if they didn't open the gaps like they did today, [the win] wouldn't have happened. We saw a lot of downfield rushing [on film], which really opened the trap because all we had to do was slide them out."

Such ground dominance soon led to an efficient passing attack from sophomore quarterback Henry Cone, especially in the second half.

"All practice; we were trying to really aim to win the line of scrimmage to get our run game going so we can pop it out for the slips, outs and even our deep comebacks," said Taumalolo, who scored from the flat off a play action in the second quarter. "[The slip out to me] is one of our main plays, we practice that every single day."

While the game certainly did not go in Rocori's favor, the bad became worse as injuries started to pile up.

Sophomore quarterback Tyson Zauhar went down in the fourth quarter with a cramp. Senior linebacker Renner Haven went down on the final drive with a sprained ankle, according to Larson.

"Losing week one sucks," Larson said. "We felt like there's just some plays here and there, like we [would] execute and [then] turn the ball over. Those were big momentum swingers. As an offense, we just got to protect the football and do our job that we've been coaching throughout the whole week. It's just growing pains that we got to work through, and we will."

Rocori is back in action Sept. 11 at Marshall.

articles.title: Huntington falls to Portsmouth West, shifts focus to Zane Trace
articles.summary: After a loss to Portsmouth West to cap its non-league schedule, Huntington is shifting its focus to an important game at Zane Trace.
articles.body:
There's no time for Huntington to dwell on Friday night (Sept. 4).

Put simply, the Huntsmen couldn't contain Portsmouth West's two-headed backfield monster of Anthony Bishop and Westyn Ratcliff in a 28-7 loss.

The Senators' dynamic duo combined to rush for 366 yards and four scores.

But the sun will come up Saturday morning with Huntington facing forward instead of looking in the rearview mirror.

"All of our goals are ahead of us. I know tonight didn't go our way but our kids will learn from the mistakes," Huntington coach Clay Beeler said. "I'm already over it. The team's over it. I guarantee you that these guys are going to come back ready to battle tomorrow. We're still a great football team and we're still healthy. We just have to put some things together to play with teams like Portsmouth West."

From the get-go, the Senators (3-0) called on Bishop to do their dirty work.

The hard-nosed, yet elusive tailback put Portsmouth West on the board at the 6:17 mark in the first quarter, making it 7-0 with a five-yard run.

Huntington (1-2) provided an answer with 5:01 remaining in the second, thanks to a 30-yard touchdown strike from Frankie Hirsch to Junior McDonald.

But Bishop was just getting started. With just 1:23 before halftime, he'd score again from seven yards out to send the Senators into the break with a 14-7 advantage.

"[West] has great running backs, obviously," Beeler said. "But I just thought we didn't tackle well, and I thought penalties killed us in the first half. We made some adjustments and got two or three stops in the second half. But offensively, they ate us up in the box. We were behind the sticks all night. It's just small things that we have to fix."

Bishop scored a third time with 8:35 left in the third and, with 10:53 remaining in the game, Ratcliff provided the knockout punch with an 85-yard rushing touchdown.

Huntington kept fighting to get back into the contest, but it was to no avail.

"We didn't quit. Our kids battled," Beeler said. "We're down 28-7 late and we got a fourth down stop to get the ball back. So our kids didn't quit and we stayed disciplined tonight. West was just big up front and we didn't tackle well. When you don't tackle well against a team that runs the ball like they do, you're in trouble."

Statistically, Hirsch led the Huntsmen, going 8-of-17 passing for 119 yards and a touchdown while also adding 11 rushes for 40 yards. McDonald caught five passes for 79 yards and a score.

Defensively, Carson McNeal and Wes Hamilton each had nine tackles.

The Huntsmen will face another stiff challenge on Sept. 11, traveling to Kinnikinnick to take on a Zane Trace program that has yet to be beaten.

The Pioneers will also bring in a strong run game that's been their centerpiece this fall.

"We have a sign in the locker room that says, 'Do your job.' If 11 guys do their job, great things happen. If 10 guys do their job, bad things happen," Beeler said. "We played West because we felt like they would prepare us for Zane Trace. Now, we've played a big, physical offensive line with great running backs. We'll be ready next week. Our kids will put in work and we'll give [Zane Trace] everything we've got."

articles.title: Five takeaways from USC’s 39-0 victory over Fresno State
articles.summary: What did we learn from watching the Trojans improve to 2-0 on Friday?
articles.body:
On Friday, the USC football's victory team defeated Fresno State 39-0 at the Coliseum . With the victory, the Trojans improved to 2-0 on the 2026 season.

What did we learn from the game? Here are five key takeaways:

Unlike last week, USC did not take its foot off the gas in the fourth quarter. This time, the Trojans played a full 60 minutes of football and did not allow their opponent to make the game look closer than it actually was with several garbage time scores.

Is Fresno State an elite opponent? Absolutely not. But shutting out any team in college football is not easy. Defensive coordinator Gary Patterson deserves his flowers for this performance.

Trent Mosley might already be one of the best wide receivers in the country. For the second consecutive game, he recorded over 100 yards receiving and also found the end zone—this time, doing it twice.

USC quarterback Jayden Maiava had perhaps his best statistical performance as a Trojan to date. Playing less than three full quarters of action, Maiava completed 23 of 25 pass attempts for 349 yards and three touchdowns. On the season, USC's quarterback now has as many total touchdowns (six) as incompletions.

Have you ever seen a defense record not one, but two safeties in a single game? Well, the Trojans did just that!

After a short week this past week, USC will now have an extra day off before hosting Louisiana next Saturday night at the Coliseum. Kickoff is set for 8:00 p.m. Pacific time on Big Ten Network.

articles.title: Andy Ruiz Jr vs Damian Knyba: LIVE round-by-round and results!
articles.summary: Andy Ruiz Jr looks to reignite his career against Damian Knyba plus more TONIGHT!
articles.body:
Former heavyweight titlist Andy Ruiz Jr will look to get his career moving tonight, when he returns to face Damian Knyba in the main event of this month's "The Fight" on DAZN and TNT.

Bad Left Hook will be here from 8 pm ET with live results, reactions, and more, including round-by-round updates for the main event and chief support on the undercard, which will see Vito Mielnicki Jr face Austin "Ammo" Williams in what is really a must-win fight for both middleweights.

It's a four-fight card in all, and we'll also have the live chat rolling down in the comments section, so join us and your fellow fight fans tonight!

Damian Knyba def. Andy Ruiz Jr by Unanimous Decision

Official Scores: 114-113, 114-113, 117-110 for Knyba

Post-Fight Thoughts: Those two 114-113 cards for Knyba are disgraceful and without the knockdown Knyba scored, this would have been a majority draw or possibly even flipped to a Ruiz victory. Ruiz (35-3-1, 22 KO) didn't win this fight and didn't have any argument to have won it. Glenn Feldman and Kevin Morgan were scoring on what, brand name? Because Ruiz did next to nothing in nine or 10 of these rounds. The slower rounds are pretty hard to not give to Knyba (18-1, 11 KO), who doesn't really leave this fight looking like a serious heavyweight contender, but at least his jab was SOMETHING while Ruiz was doing nothing. Andy Ruiz is nearly 37 and hasn't impressed in a fight in over seven years. We'll have more shortly on the front page , so check back then, and thank you for joining us tonight!

Round 12: Ruiz trying again early in the round, but he just can't get to Knyba. Feet are too slow, too heavy. And he doesn't have the hand speed and whatnot that made up for that in his prime. He's trying in this round. Knyba is mostly trying to jab and stay clear of any hope for Andy to land a home run shot. And what hurts Andy is he's never been some huge puncher, either. He can punch, but that wasn't what stood out for him. He lost this fight. Knyba 10-9, 118-109

Round 11: Yeah, back to what we've seen most of the night. Well, no, Andy starting to throw a bit more again, but then he isn't. No urgency. Because he can't get the timing and Knyba is moving around at distance. Andy can't close him down quick enough. Big right from Knyba! Uppercut thrown but missed, Andy comes up with a hook that gets mostly blocked. Knyba 10-9, 108-100

Round 10: Ruiz continuing to come forward. Not as urgent as you might want to see, maybe, but also may not be able to produce that for any number of reasons. Knyba starting to get back to his jab this round and Ruiz not having the success he'd had in the prior two. The B-side Knyba is back in control this round, back into the rhythm. Knyba 10-9, 98-91

Round 9: This is the first Round 9 that Knyba has ever seen. If I still gambled, I would absolutely put a small bet on Ruiz right now before the odds narrow. Not saying he'll win, but there are some things that favor him from here. And he's getting more aggressive. The knockdown seems like it has woken Andy up a little. Andy landing right hands, moving forward, but not wasting energy. He looks a little more confident again. Body shot from Ruiz. Knyba's jab has gone away and the right hands don't have much zip on them. He may have emptied his own tank far more than he's used to when he tried to get that stoppage. Ruiz 10-9, Knyba 88-82

Round 8: Ruiz being told if he gets in trouble again the fight will be stopped. Knyba jabbing hard to start the round, Ruiz trying to throw his hands but it's desperation now. Right hand from Knyba. Ruiz trying to time something. Jabs snapping his head back. Another right comes in. But Ruiz does land a good shot and that pushes Knyba back a bit, and he's on the back foot. Ruiz is showing some fire in this round, and I think he hurt Knyba again late to the body. This was Ruiz's best round. Ruiz 10-9, Knyba 79-72

Round 7: Truthfully, I don't think Ruiz has the hand speed that used to be special for a heavyweight. We're not seeing any combinations. And while his feet were always heavy, he still doesn't move as well as he used to. BIG SHOT AND KNYBA HAS HIM HURT! RUIZ GETTING ROCKED AND HE'S DOWN HARD! Ruiz is up but his legs are gone. They should stop this. Referee giving him "one more shot." Long recovery time, too. Knyba nails him again but Ruiz barely survives the round. Knyba 10-8, 70-62

Round 6: There's a good right from Andy about a minute in, he finally was able to land one "between" the punches from Knyba. Best punch of the night from him, at least to the head, maybe a body shot earlier was better. Knyba may have a little cut outside the left eye, too — yeah, he does. But Knyba back to bouncing and jabbing. Ruiz doesn't have the legs to keep pace with that. Not sure the low-rise trunks are helping either. But that's another story. And after the one good right hand it's back to Jab and Hop: The Damian Knyba Story . This was a deeply discouraging non-performance from Andy Ruiz in the first half. Knyba 10-9, 60-54

Round 5: Andy now sort of caught up in trying to disrupt the holding quickly. Still not really doing anything effectively. Now sort of windmilling his arms at Knyba. Knyba being warned for holding, though, and if that gets more serious it could change the fight. Because Knyba is using that as a nullifier, for sure. Already you can see Knyba now moving more and not staying in place willing to grab. Ruiz is showing these little signals that he's alive in there but then nothing is happening behind that. He's just not successfully doing anything so far. And he's frustrated in a way that has him starting to look sad between rounds. Knyba 10-9, 50-45

Round 4: There is nothing in what Ruiz is doing here through three but you can see him making some moves in the 4th, even if it's out of frustration it's a sign of life. Knyba's holding when Ruiz does get close to him. And it's still winning rounds. Knyba 10-9, 40-36

Round 3: Ruiz has not showed any combination punching at all to this point. Granted it's very early, but this is what Knyba wants the fight to be. If he can get it to stay this way, it's going to be hard for Ruiz to win. He's just losing these rounds because he isn't doing near enough and Knyba is dictating. It's on "small" work, but it's effective, and nothing Ruiz is doing is. Knyba 10-9, 30-27

Round 2: Manny Robles wants Ruiz to look to the body, which does seem to be another obvious idea. Andy struggling to get there, though. Knyba keeping that jab moving, even just when it's flicking out there. Ruiz throws the right to the body, Knyba takes a half-step back and jabs away again. Ruiz shoots an overhand right. But he's struggling to get any momentum going here and the Knyba jab, albeit nothing devastating or whatever, is dictating the tempo entirely. Knyba 10-9, 20-18

Round 1: Knyba clearly wants to use his length and work behind the jab early. Obvious idea, and he's trying to do it. He is significantly taller and longer than Ruiz, and he could be a minor puzzle. And I think he won a mostly unevenftul first round, because Ruiz just couldn't get inside at all, and jabs beat, like, nothing. Knyba 10-9

Preview: It's been over seven years since the last time Andy Ruiz (35-2-1, 22 KO) really impressed anyone. He's always been a lot better "than he looks," has always been dramatically more skilled than you'd think at a glance. Still is, really. But he's also about to turn 37 and has basically been half-in the game for this entire decade. Beating washed Chris Arreola and ancient Luis Ortiz, drawing with Big Baby Miller — it's just been a long time since you could really see Ruiz as a top contender. This is Comeback #4 in the last five years, this time it's serious, and so on. We'll see. He should be favored here, though. Knyba (17-1, 11 KO) does have big height and reach advantages, but if Ruiz isn't shot I think Andy should win fairly handily. But you never know! Sometimes it's just gone when fighters get so inconsistent with their schedule. They show up for another one and it's just not there anymore.

Vito Mielnicki Jr def. Austin "Ammo" Williams by Unanimous Decision

Official Scores: 98-91, 98-91, 98-91 for Mielnicki

Post-Fight Thoughts: The best performance of the 24-year-old Mielnicki's career, as he improves to 24-1 (13 KO) with a fine win over a guy who has been in or around the top 10 at 160 for a while. 160 is weak, sure, and Ammo (20-3, 13 KO) is a very flawed fighter with beyond leaky defense, but Mielnicki has really come into his own. If you last saw him as a large child on the PBC FOX shows, give him a fresher assessment. This is not that same kid. He showed some toughness, he's dramatically improved under Ronnie Shields, he's grown and matured. He's a legitimate contender now — in an admittedly weak division, but a legitimate contender all the same. He should be very happy with this win, and I think he showed us some of his own toughness, the grit that wasn't yet there, understandably, when he was a teenager.

Round 10: Both guys have been told to go out and fight. Could be ready for some dramatics. But Vito's hurting Ammo! Back-to-back uppercuts! But Ammo throwing shots back. The uppercuts from Vito just keep landing! Both hands! Body shot from Vito, good punch. Another right up top. Check hook lands. Ammo just has nothing left, he put what he had into the previous two rounds. But he just keeps eating punches, he is an exceptionally tough guy. Mielnicki keeps landing as it winds down. He put an exclamation point on it. Mielnicki 10-9, 97-92

Round 9: Ammo tells his corner that he knows he needs a KO. And he's the kind of guy who will try to get it, too. We'll see how Vito does if Ammo starts really pressing for it. Mielnicki's sneaky good at using his elbow to create space; he's not really fouling with it, but he gets it in there and buys himself a moment. Vito doing a good job of avoiding big shots this round, but little real offense coming back from him. And it's smart, really. I don't have to like it as a fight fan, but I get what he wants to do. And then Ammo lands another good shot, Mielnicki scampers away when he can. You could probably argue Vito quietly sneaking this round because he did some good work, but I'm nicking it to Ammo. Williams 10-9, Mielnicki 87-83

Round 8: Well, Ammo lands a real good shot coming out this round. He's needed that. Can he follow up now? And he walks into a little check hook from Vito, but Ammo keeps marching forward. Whatever you think of his flaws, he is a tough, tough dude. And he's got Vito's nose bleeding. And Vito is starting to get a little stationary and looking more worried. The crowd is changing — Ammo is having real success this round. You can feel the energy shifting. Vito trying to jab and settle it down some. Williams 10-9, Mielnicki 78-73

Round 7: Williams really needs to find something big, and soon. He's struggling pretty badly and Mielnicki is keeping things simple and effective, when he sees chances he presses a bit but he's not fighting dumb, ever. And he just keeps landing solid shots on Williams, whose defense looks worse than ever and was always his biggest problem. And this was probably Ammo's best round in a while, you could maybe argue it for him. Mielnicki 10-9, 69-63

Round 6: Ammo just keeps walking into and eating shots, but Williams is really trying hard to find something meaningful and slug his way back into this. But he doesn't seem to be bothering Mielnicki or scaring him with anything that comes in. Mielnicki 10-9, 59-54

Round 5: Ammo hurt big with about a minute and change left, in a round Vito had been winning but not dominating or anything. Mielnicki just looks stronger and, more importantly, far less shopworn. I can't ignore that. Ammo came into this one off of a beating and he's taking another one. He got cracked again a couple times late and he does not look good going back to the corner. Mielnicki 10-9, 49-45

Round 4: Vito trying to pick up where he left off in the second half of Round 3. Ammo touching him, but Vito answering. Mielnicki getting around the ring near the ropes now, then moves back toward the center. He's trying to get Ammo to chase a bit, but isn't afraid to move forward, either. Williams keeps loading up big on that left hand, and it's missing. Good right hand shot from Vito, right down the middle. Stats have Mielnicki landing just under 60% of his power shots so far, and that's hard to overcome. Ammo hurt again on a right hand! Uppercut comes under a missed left hand, another good shot for Ammo! Williams is a tough dude but he got rocked around again here. Mielnicki 10-9, 39-36

Round 3: Williams looking like he's gotten a little confidence back. Now that can be a good thing or a bad thing with guys who are defensively flawed like Ammo. But he's working away and evening things up a bit right now. Some decent body shots. And then warned for going low with one. Vito looking to the body now, too. Vito seeing some openings again as the round wears on, first half of the round probably was Ammo's, second half looks like Vito's so far. So a close round! Williams really wants that right hook, and he's getting pretty close with it. Shade the round to Mielnicki, who landed another good shot late. Mielnicki 10-9, 29-27

Round 2: Ammo with a decent shot early in the round, trying to get his feet back, trying to get some respect back. He's not out of this fight or anything, it's very early. And he's landing some more solid shots, and looking to make a difference. I thought Ammo won this round, landed the better shots, calmed down, isn't gonna fold. Williams 10-9, Mielnicki 19-18

Round 1: Good right early from Mielnicki. They're staying center ring. Mielnicki circling into the left hand of southpaw Williams, which Mora notes is usually wrong but against Williams does work. DOWN GOES AMMO WILLIAMS AND HE'S HURT BAD! Got up too fast, but he's trying to take the count more in the corner. Great shot that Ammo just ran into! But Ammo lands a shot that pushes Mielnicki back a bit, too! Vito got him again and he's pressing for it here! Ammo trying to stay calm and find an opening for a counter, to get Vito to run into one like he did. Jersey crowd chanting for home state Mielnicki. Mielnicki 10-8

Preview: Mielnicki (23-1, 13 KO) was given too hard of a push back when PBC was on FOX, yet had no budget so they tried to focus on young, undercooked prospects they thought would draw eyes, like Vito and Joey Spencer. Both had hope, but also looked like they might hit a low ceiling. Spencer did. Vito is still in the game. He suffered an upset loss in 2021, but bounced back. He has started to figure himself out. He was 18 in that fight, he's 24 tonight. And if he's going to grow into being an actual contender, it was time to give it a go. Williams (20-2, 13 KO) is 30 and has been found wanting against Hamzah Sheeraz in 2024 and Carlos Adames earlier this year. He took a spirited beating in both fights. He needs to win this one, if he doesn't it's going to be really hard for him to really get back in the mix and not become a gatekeeper. But if he does, yeah, 160 is still open. And for Vito, this is his toughest fight yet on paper, a chance to prove he really belongs and isn't a promoter creation.

Eridson Garcia def. Alan Chaves by Unanimous Decision

Official Scores: 98-88, 99-88, 99-87 for Garcia

Post-Fight Thoughts: Huge win for Garcia (24-2, 14 KO) and a big, bubble-busting setback for Chaves (22-1, 19 KO). Chaves had a massive disadvantage in reach, he's kind of small at 135, and he it was a big problem that he couldn't do anything about. I do think, as many have already suspected, that Chaves had a nose issue from early on, and he was very tough in there, but he was dropped four times and just totally dominated overall. Garcia had his number and Chaves never had an answer. This fight was designed to make Chaves a top contender at 135; that is not what Matchroom got from it in the end.

Total domination from Eridson Garcia in what should be a clear, unquestionable upset victory. BLH Unofficial Score: 99-87 for Eridson Garcia

Chaves down for a fourth time in Round 9. Again gets out of the round. This has been an awful night for Alan Chaves, but the man is tough. He's proven that. That's about it, being brutally honest.

After Round 8, the NJ commision has reviewed the slip and ruled it a slip. Could totally swing that round from 10-8 Chaves to 10-9 Garcia. I do love that the judges are now being asked to remember how they felt about an uneventful round from about 10 minutes ago. Great system.

Garcia ruled down early in Round 6 on what appeared to clearly be a slip. Remainder of the round is uneventful. BoxRec study in the future will make that seem like a lot more success than Chaves has had so far. He didn't even actually land a punch there. Garcia slipped on obvious water on the canvas.

Chaves down AGAIN. About a minute left in Round 5 and will try to continue. He does, and he makes the end of the round, but this has become one-way traffic.

Chaves down again early in Round 5! He's hurting in there. He gets up but Garcia is completely dominant so far.

Chaves was rocked pretty hard again right before the end of Round 4. This is getting increasingly one-sided. Chaves fighting like he just doesn't have ideas.

We're three rounds in and Chaves is having a terrible time with Garcia. Chaves has the power to still be dangerous but Garcia came in here with a great plan and is executing it.

Garcia with a nice opening round and now Chaves is down in Round 2! He's up but he got nailed there, he's struggling with the reach of Garcia.

Preview: Chaves (22-0, 19 KO) is 25, southpaw, out of Argentina, might be a real contender at 135. He's got some decent wins and looks good on the eye test, he can punch, and he smashed Miguel Madueno in his first fight away from home in April, good to see him back pretty quickly and continuing to try and build his name in the States. Garcia (23-2, 14 KO) was a Zuffa hopeful who appears free to roam after his loss to Andres Cortes in April. I didn't think Garcia did poorly in that fight or anything, but he's a fairly low-ceiling guy. Still, has to be taken seriously here; he did upset Taiga Imanaga in Riyadh, and he's scored some decent wins. He can fight! I think this is a pretty nice matchup to be third from the top on this show. He also has a crazy reach advantage in this fight.

Zaquin Moses def. Angel Antonio Contreras by TKO after Round 5

Post-Fight Thoughts: Fine performance from young Moses, now 8-0 (4 KO). His corner was pressing him to go for the stoppage if the sixth round had started, but it didn't, the corner pulled the plug after five. I think commentary called Contreras (18-11-2, 12 KO) "The Tough Mexican" about 30 times in the five rounds we got. He came here to fight, but the class difference was obvious and just too much, and even if Moses is not a huge puncher, he was doing damage to the body especially. He's a cool, confident young fighter, doesn't hunt for knockouts, believes in his skills, but also doesn't fight arrogantly.

It's over! Contreras' corner pulls the plug after five rounds. Moses TKO-5

We're through four rounds. The gulf in talent is, as expected, very wide. Moses has done some nice body work.

Zaquin landed one of the most incredible super-low blow/head butt combos you'll ever see in the opening round.

Fight's about to start. Harvey Dock is your referee.

Preview: Should be a typical Prospect vs Guy fight, Moses (7-0, 3 KO) is the 21-year-old cousin of Shakur Stevenson, and also a Newark native, so he's on home turf and also here to sell some tickets. Legit prospect, not sure if he's some super blue chipper or anything like that. Contreras (18-10-2, 12 KO) is a 32-year-old journeyman from Monterrey, Mexico, has won two straight but at very low level. But he's tested a lot of good prospects — Bruce Carrington, Michael Angeletti, Justin Viloria, Albert "Chop Chop" Gonzalez — and he tends to go the distance.

Location: Prudential Center – Newark, NJ
